utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are about five or six documents, so I can't be 100 per cent sure, but I don't believe that Vasic sent copies of these reports to the Special Police in Bijeljina. I think -- I could stand to be corrected, but I believe you're -- you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that is my own assertion, but now I just want to confirm that the MUP didn't send this to Borovcanin. Did you see any one of these telegrams containing Mr. Borovcanin as an addressee, these telegrams sent from Mr. Vasic from the Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There were several documents and there were references to Borovcanin in at least one of them, so the question is misstating the evidence and it, in order to get a proper answer, needs to be seen, all of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was just referring to the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a specific document in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- that were used during the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There was a number of them, and perhaps we can cut it short. I would tend to agree that they are not addressed to him, but as you know, that's not where the story stops, and so the question is slightly misleading in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely my question, whether they were addressed to Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think if you have in mind a specific document, you can go straight to that document and perhaps rephrase your question, but I think that we can safely go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So in order to do away with any dilemma, did you see any telegram sent from Vasic that had been sent directly to Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not have been addressed to him, given he didn't have the material ability or lack of a command post to receive them. Like I said, I don't believe any of the documents that are attributed to Vasic, you know, specifically list him as an addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is what I had wanted to ask you. Also, you don't have any examples to the contrary; namely, that Mr. Borovcanin submitted some kind of reports to Vasic. You didn't come across any such documents, Borovcanin sending documents to Vasic, or, rather, reports to Vasic, sorry?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean, I don't -- I'm not aware of any documents which reflect Colonel Borovcanin reporting in a formal text manner or anything to Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So between the two of them, there is no relationship based on subordination and a superior position, not in any sense?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the events and the resubordination, you know, certainly during the period of 12, 13 and 14 July, and even on 15, when they move up to Zvornik, there is not a document that I'm aware of where Colonel Borovcanin is subordinated to Dragan Vasic, or vice versa, for that matter. Only those units that were already previously designated from the CSB, which would be Vasic's people, to the command of Colonel Borovcanin, those are the only documents I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was my question. During your testimony here, namely, on the 16th of January, 2008, and the page is 19814 of the transcript, when you gave your comments on Mr. Vasic's telegram, you said that on the 12th of July, 1995, before the meeting with the UN forces -- before the third meeting, I do apologise, a meeting was indeed held of several VRS and police commanders. You used the plural here when you talked about commanders of the police. And on that occasion, General Mladic and General Krstic gave certain tasks to the units. Do you remember that part of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe that is -- my testimony in that regard is a direct lift from a Vasic document. I think it's dated about 12 July at 8.00 in the morning, if I recall correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the context of your answer related to that document. However, this is my following question: While preparing your expert reports and while you analysed documents, did you find anywhere information to the effect that Mr. Borovcanin was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall if he's listed in that particular document or not, and I'd like to see the document again, if I could. I mean, I don't know that he is or isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get clarification on "meetings"? I think there were a few meetings that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have P00059.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see any reference to Mr. Borovcanin here, in terms of his attendance at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not, and at present I don't recall whether, in his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, whether or not he indicated that he was present at this meeting or not, so I don't -- the answer is I don't have any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Just one more question in relation to this, and then we're going to move on to another topic. Did you come across any information, in the documents that you reviewed, to the effect that in the period between the 11th and 13th of July, Mr. Borovcanin was present at any meeting with the higher officers of the VRS there in the field?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the context of any information, the way I would answer it is that given that he was required to coordinate his activities with the military and that he has acknowledged receiving instructions, you know, in his statement to the OTP from, at least on one occasion, General Mladic as to where his forces needed to be, he was looped into the information process with that regard. Now, whether it was actually within the context of a formalised meeting or meetings, I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I was interested in specific meetings, but I am satisfied with the answer that you gave. Now I would like to move on to another topic. During your testimony, you said that due to the fact that the army was at a completely different location and due to the fact that there weren't sufficient combat forces in the field, on the 12th of July, certain MUP units were sent along this road. And the page reference is 19816, dated the 16th of January, 2008. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I remember talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I prepared a large number of documents and a lot of material that I'd like us to go through with respect to certain facts. However, since my time is limited, first I'm going to suggest certain facts to you. And if we agree on them, then there will be no need to go through all of these documents. Now I would like to have a look at document 4D141.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask for the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Butler, this document is a map that involves the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road as well as Mount Udrc, the broader area. In order to make it easier for you to find your way, there are red markings on this map of the command post and positions and movement of VRS and MUP RS units. What I have to say, for the sake of precision, is that there is an omission on this map. A military police squad that was in Konjevic Polje at the time has been omitted, it is not marked here. Also, blue arrows were used to denote the movement of the movement of the 28th Division of the BH Army as stated in Ramiz Becirovic's statement, and dotted blue arrows denote expected movements on the basis of the intelligence that the Drina Corps had at the time. As you can see on the map, it is the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I see the date on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. These markings on the map, are you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen the map before, but I am familiar with the -- with what the markings represent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Of course, you could not have seen this map this way, because it was prepared by this Defence over the course of the past few days. But now I would like to ask you something else. During your testimony, you said that you were familiar with the direction of movement of the 28th Division of the BH Army, and when you look at these markings, when you look at where they're going, these are the circles denoting the area of disposition of some brigades, this is the area of Mount Udrc, the arrow there, does this precisely depict the route taken by the 28th Division towards Udrc?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my information, I believe that it is an accurate representation of the routes and the crossing points, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get precisely who did this map so we know something more about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We did it, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, as I understood Mr. Lazarevic, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was prepared by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not very precise. I would like to know, is it a military expert, is it a lawyer, you know, who is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if you want to give the information. It's being asked of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can provide information, based on certain documents that we had in our case, in consultation of course with some military person, and of course in cooperation with our client, we made this map all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that suffices.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That was -- that was my point. Obviously, it's going to be offered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you're right, Mr. McCloskey. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This second dotted blue line that goes in the direction of Kuslat, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that this was the assumed line that the 28th Division was supposed to take on the basis of information contained in document P111, dated the 12th of July, 1995? If you wish, you can have a look at that document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate that, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then see P111, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document is a document of the Intelligence Department of the Drina Corps Command, dated 12 July 1995, and I found it very interesting to draw this map, and I'm referring to the last part in B/C/S where it says: "While able-bodied formations started breaking towards Tuzla, probably across Ravni Buljin, Purkovica, Kusleta and further on across Udrc, Kozjak, Kamenica, Crni Vrh, Nezuk." Would that be the axis that reflects what is written in the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It could help us -- if Ravni Buljin is noted on the document, that might help him. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just -- I'm just kind of lacking reference points between the first point in Kuslat, so I have no way of knowing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't see Jaglici, Susnjari, so tough question to ask him with a map that's missing key points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will not insist on this question. Maybe we'll have an occasion to see some other maps later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to put to you at the moment, which you can also see on the map, is that the forces of Mr. Borovcanin arrived at the road only in the evening of the 12th of July, which means around 2000 hours or after that time; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I could accept that completely. My understanding is that at least one company of the Jahorina Training Centre was at Konjevic Polje on 12 July earlier than that. I am aware that other formations that were down as far as Potocari were redeployed later that day, but I -- but I have information that indicates that there were members of at least the Jahorina -- one of the Jahorina police companies at Konjevic Polje earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In any case, you can confirm that the 1st Company of the PJP and the 2nd Detachment of the Sekovici Brigade did not arrive before 2000 hours?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that by the early evening hours, they were ordered up there. I can't tell you exactly when they would have arrived by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. One more question that arises from this. I'm also putting it to you that the MUP units under the command of Mr. Borovcanin arrived -- or came in contact with the 28th Division of the BH Army only on the 13th of July, at 4.00 in the morning, in the Sandici-Konjevic Polje sector when one or two people were killed and two or three wounded. Would you accept that, as I put it to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that there was at least one police officer who was killed up on the road during the evening hours of the 12th. I don't recall whether he was a member of that or whether he was part of one of the other PJP companies operating outside of Colonel Borovcanin's control. Certainly by about 3.00 or 4.00 in the morning, those police companies would have been encountering lead elements of the column. So that would be 0304 in the morning, they would have been in contact with the column, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe I have to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On page 19 -- on page 62, line 19, it should read "on the 13th of July at 4.00 in the morning."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's lines 19 and 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Your Honour. Yes. And in further, in line 20, same page, it should read "Sandici-Konjevic Polje sector."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P00062.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already seen this document. Can we now look at the first paragraph, where it says: "In the early morning hours of 13 July 1995 (at about 0400 hours), the 1st PJP Zvornik came in contact ...," and so on and so forth. Isn't this precisely what I suggested to you, i.e., that at around 4.00 in the morning, that unit had their first contact with the enemy column?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that location, the 1st PJP Company, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we look at another map, which is Exhibit number 4D00142, and again this is a map that was prepared by the Defence. Basically, it's the same map as the one that we had before, with the only difference being that this one bears the date 13 July 1995. The participants are the same, the locations are the same. Can you please briefly look at the map, and then I'm going to have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you compared the map depicting the previous date, the 12th of July, with the map depicting the 13th of July, can we then say that the blue circles around "Kamenica" represent the remains of the 28th Division and also one part at the foot of Udrc Mountain in the left part of the map, would that correspond to the information that you had?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that the lead elements of the 28th crossed the road the late evening of the 12th, the early morning of the 13th. Your blue symbol there to designate the remnants and the arrow that they're pointing is a little bit too vague for me to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just a few more things about this map I would like to clarify with you. The red arrows in the lower part of the map, the wide arrows, indicate the direction of scouring the terrain in that part which was carried out by the 1st Milici Infantry Brigade [Realtime transcript read in error "1st Military Brigade"] and the Bratunac Brigade on the 13th of July; would that be correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if they were actually that far from the operations orders, but those were -- at least the general axes were projected sweep axes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could we get another question? "1st Military Brigade," I don't think that's what you said, so if that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's Milici Brigade. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you both, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Lazarevic, just for the record, you confirm that this map was prepared in the same circumstances as the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now can we clarify one more thing. Can we look at P00245 in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document bears the date 13 July 1995. Under bullet point 2, it says: "The main forces of the Bratunac Brigade continue to scour the terrain in the ordered direction of Ravni Buljin-Zvijezda-Siljato Brdo. Some of the forces are engaged in crushing enemy forces which have retreated to the aforementioned sector." Does this description help you to locate the Bratunac Brigade on the map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am generally aware where the Bratunac Brigade was, but as I've noted, my understanding is that while those were planned axes of advance with respect to Bratunac, that they had not achieved certainly the far end of those lines. They didn't wander very far away from their initial trench positions. It wasn't until the 14th when you will get a subsequent order that, in much greater detail, defines that sweep operation, giving them -- giving them more detailed objectives. So, I mean, the axis is clear, but I think we're a day early on the actual implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's just confirm one thing, please, and I'm talking about Konjevic Polje here. If you've looked at the map bearing the date 12th of July, the unit that was in Konjevic Polje was the 2nd Company of the PJP, apparently. This time around, it is the 5th Company of the PJP. Can you just confirm for us that the 2nd PJP Company on the 12th retreated from Konjevic Polje and went to Srebrenica, where they were tasked with establishing the police force?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, if I recall the particular document in question, two platoons were withdrawn and sent to Srebrenica and one platoon remained in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, the 5th Company is the one that took over, right, replaced it, the 5th Company of the PJP, of course?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to see the document. I don't recall that, that particular fact. It may very well be in place, but I just don't recall it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we have an early break and continue later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Are you on track? Are you on track, time-wise? All right. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Butler, we shall continue where we stopped. But just briefly, prior to that, can we go back to map 4D141 showing the situation as on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can I have the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Butler, I shall ask you just a few short questions now, because you have already had occasion to see this map. These questions concern the disposition of forces. Can you confirm that in the right-hand lower corner, the positions of the Bratunac Brigade are indicated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions of the headquarters of the 4th Battalion and the 1st Battalion correspond to locations that I know them to be. Yes, those are their headquarters locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then further on to the left from the positions of the Bratunac Brigade is the position of the Milici Brigade, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, to the left and, map-wise, to the southwest, is the zone of the Milici Brigade, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just another thing. The 28th Division practically passed through the positions of the Milici and Bratunac Brigades, according to what is indicated here with the arrow, and continued along this axis that you have already pointed to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The -- the column actually did go out in an area that corresponded with the brigade boundaries, so it kind of cut the seam.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, exactly. I shall just put another two or three questions in this connection to you. Can you confirm that a battalion of the military police of the 65th Protective Regiment was located at Nova Kasaba, which is to say exactly as indicated on this map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, I understand that the battalion headquarters was located in the school at Nova Kasaba, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At the crossroads in Konjevic Polje was the 5th Engineers Battalion, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The 5th Engineer Battalion of the Drina Corps, their headquarters was located in a facility. It may have been the school, I'm not exactly sure, at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the 2nd PJP Company is also there at that same location as drawn in on the map, the Zvornik PJP, of course?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- there's a notation of them there. I don't know if that's their actual -- you have them listed right along what's the Cerska River and valley. I don't know if they're actually holding a chunk of line there or whether they're up further on the road. I mean, I see where you have the notation. I just can't confirm on the ground that that's where they actually were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right, very well. If you can't, you can't. Now may we look at document P00377, please. This is a note of the operative on duty of the Zvornik Brigade. I should like to see page 114 in B/C/S and, in English, the page bearing the ERN number 0293-5732. I can read it out for you while we are waiting, but here, it has appeared on the screen. Let me just check whether it is the right page. No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's page 5 of the English translation. That's okay, that's okay, sorry. No, it's not the wrong page. It's page 5, I'm sorry. In B/C/S, it's page 117 of the document. Maybe I should read the English ERN: 0293-5731. It's page 5 of the document. Or we could simplify things and post the English translation on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a better idea. I think that's a better idea, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this portion that has been marked: [In English] "The Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road is not safe anymore."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "1955: Troops are close to the village of Kamenica-Pavlovica. The Praga is working already." And then within brackets: "Troops from Sekovici and the civilian police have not arrived yet." [Interpretation] This is the grounds upon which I'm suggesting to you that the troops from Sekovici and the civilian police have not arrived by 1905 -- 1955 to the road. Does this correspond to what you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, as I indicated, I mean, I'm aware that there was one company of the Jahorina police unit at Konjevic Polje at the time. This, again it appears to be -- it appears to be a verbal report that they've received from their 8th Battalion, which of course corresponds to the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, and their knowledge of the fact that the troops have -- or are supposed to be going up there. You know, it may very well be that, you know, they're not aware that the troops from Sekovici, and for argument's sake I'll agree that that's the 2nd Sekovici Detachment, and the civilian police haven't arrived yet. I mean, that's their awareness of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we now move on to map 4D142 that we looked at before the break. Can we take another look at it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, what I wish to deal with you, in connection with this map, is the following, and you already had occasion to see it. We contend that it was sometime around 1900 hours that the 2nd Detachment of the Special Police Brigade set off in the direction of Konjevic Polje and that in -- spent the night between the 13th and the 14th in the Konjevic Polje area. Does that correspond to what is your knowledge in connection with that particular element of this case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking -- I understand "13 July," I'm just trying to -- we're talking where the 2nd Police Detachment was from its prior location. It is your assertion that at 1900 hours, they left that position of the line and then moved towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not clear. Are we talking about the 12th or the 13th? It's not clear from the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, it may not be clear from the question, but the document refers to the 13th of July. The map, the second map, refers to the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is the 13th we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I disagree, and I think that -- and again I'm referring back to the testimony in a prior trial of one of the individuals. I believe it was Miso Stupar, that indicated that the unit, if I'm remembering correctly, that most of the 2nd Sekovici spent a good chunk of the evening hours in and around the old village of Kravica on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. As we have other different testimonies which I assume you have not had occasion to check, let it stand at that. I should like to ask another thing. If you remember, and we had the directional movement of the 28th Division, we saw it on the map, would the movement of that detachment from Sandici towards Konjevic Polje, would it, in principle, have been actually following the direction of the -- of movement of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically speaking, it would make sense for them to put that particular unit as well as mass most of their units around that particular location, the Konjevic Polje to Nova Kasaba line, because that was the funnel point by which all of the forces were crossing the road to move northwards. So it would make sense for them to want to mass their forces there, once they had identified that that was the choke point, for lack of a better word.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now if you look on this map, in the upper part, where there is a red circle marking, that is a place which is called "Drinjaca." Can you confirm that in the evening of the 14th or the night between the 14th and the 15th, members of the 2nd Detachment of the Special Brigade were indeed in Drinjaca? Can your investigations confirm that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no information one way or the other. Off the top of my head, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just ask you this: As you can see on this map, we have the mountain Udrc indicated there, drawn in there, and the 28th Division unit marked in blue. Do you have information that on the 13th of July, parts of the 28th Division that had already passed through were returning back in order to establish contact and communication with the parts that were lagging behind?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just another couple of questions in this connection. Does the name "Ramiz Becirovic" ring any bells, does it mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And of course you know that we are talking about the chief of staff of the 28th Division who, in the absence of Naser Oric, was in charge of the 28th Division, including in the military breakthrough; you are aware of that, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I should just like to say this to you: During the construction of this particular map, the Defence used inter alia a statement given by Ramiz Becirovic immediately after the events in Srebrenica. Do you know -- are you aware of the existence of such a statement given to the security organs by Ramiz Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may at some juncture have read that, if such a statement was turned over to the OTP and translated. It wouldn't surprise me that there would be one, but I don't recall any specifics of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is a quite lengthy statement, and if we were to go through it point by point, the cross would take two weeks, probably. But we shall now move on to another subject. In your testimony of the 16th of January, 2008, on page 19841 -- 841, you stated that the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska had three components; public security, special police units, and state security. Do you recall that answer of yours, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, those are my understanding of what the main components are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you know, you have already told us that you were no expert on the subject, that you did not in particular study the structure of the MUP, of the Ministry of the Interior, so if I told you that according to the legislation and rules then in force, and specific regulations governing the matter, the Special Brigade of the police was under the Public Security Department and that the MUP only had in fact two departments [as interpreted], that of public security and that of state security, what do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says "two departments" and I believe it's "two components" on page 73, line 4. Pages 73 -- no, it's not "two companies," it's "two components." "Components." I'm sorry for my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That may be the case, but my understanding, from reading various statements of individuals, is that they viewed it as three separate ones and that the Special Police Brigade was a separate component, it was not folded under the broader public security. So, I mean, while it may be the case, and I certainly could stand to be corrected on that if you show me the material, that's not my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but that would certainly mean that we have to take a look at evidence 4D00136. This is the Law on Internal Affairs, revised text, published in the Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska on the 18th of August, 1995. We do not have the English translation, at least not an official one, so that the Defence has prepared a draft version, a draft translation version, which I should like to show to Mr. Butler. [In English] If I can have the assistance of Madam Usher, and I have enough copies for all the participants. [Interpretation] I should like us to look at Articles 14 and 18 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see the Article 14 of the law regulates or, rather, says to discharge work and duties of public security in the Ministry there exists a Department of Public Security as a specifically-organised department. That is Article 14. And Article 18, paragraph 2, says to discharge work and duties of state security, in the Ministry there is a Department of State Security as a specifically-organised department.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but it doesn't specifically note in here your assertion that, one, those two departments are exclusive in total and doesn't discuss anything about the Special Security Brigade, is the first matter, of course. And, second, it's probably not something I would have reviewed, given the fact that this law post-dates the events that I was investigating with respect to Srebrenica 1995. My understanding of how they were organised is based off of interviews of individuals who were discussing the context of July 1995. So I don't dispute your fact, but I don't see it evident in this law, and I don't know that it wasn't changed. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to make this clear for you, the date of this law, which is the 18th of August, 1995, is the time when the revised text of the Law on Internal Affairs was published, so this is the date when all the amendments to that law were actually published, with that date inclusive. And you can see in the heading that it incorporates different amendments from 1992, 1993, 1994. That is just to clarify this matter. Is this of any assistance to you in order for us to actually establish that it was a law that was applicable and valid at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I hold open the possibility. However, before I could really definitively take a look at it, I would need to see the base laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We shall not pursue the matter further. We still have two topics to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can P01140A, the exhibit of that number, be shown to the witness. This is an intercept of the 13th of July, 1350 [as interpreted] hours. I apologise. The transcript says "1350". It's actually 1530.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Mr. Butler, you have already given testimony here about this intercept, do you recall that, and you said that the concept "Utucac" [phoen] was unfamiliar and that you weren't sure that this intercept concerned Ljubomir Borovcanin or any other Borovcanin, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is on pages which the interpreter could not catch. Could the counsel kindly repeat the pages. It was said too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you hear what the interpreter --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 19893 are the pages and 19894. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, first and foremost, do you recall that portion of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If you do remember Exhibit 4D142, the map that we had occasion to see, do you remember that the Mount Udrc was drawn in on that map, and it was drawn in as the place where the forces of the 28th Division were on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see where you have -- where it's on the map, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on the 12th of July, the column was moving along the [indiscernible] and so on direction and then through Udrc towards Kozluk and on; that was the direction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Kozluk? I mean, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Towards Nezuk. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the general axis of the column was through that particular area, Udrc towards Nezuk. At least the lead portion of the column was going towards that direction. If I recall correctly, their initial -- after breaking out of the southern area, their initial assembly area was at Udrc, or that it would then set the stage to begin the next part, which would be towards the Nezuk area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you have already exhausted the two hours that you had asked for. Will you bring your cross-examination to an end as soon as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll do my best. However, these are highly relevant issues. I was really trying my best to speed up things, but with some documents it's simply not possible. And the only issues that I need to cover with the witness are intercepts which are relevant for our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go quickly through that and try and finish. And we need about five minutes at the end for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, with regard to the conversation that we have just had -- seen, if in this case the person in question is Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin, would you allow for a possibility that somebody is sending Mr. Borovcanin to Udrc, to the mountain, in order to engage in a battle with the 28th Division column which at that moment was advancing towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking -- we're talking 13 July; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, yes, and the time is 1530 hours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean, I have no information whatsoever that would substantiate that or could be used to lend weight to that theory. The information that I'm aware of places them and keeps them on that road on 13 July, so I can't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't put it to you that he actually did it. I was putting to you that somebody might have asked from him to send those forces towards the mountain, towards Udrc, in order to engage the 28th Division. Does that make any military logic at all?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've testified, because this conversation is so fragmentary, that I really can't make any assessment on what it does or doesn't mean. Would it make sense in the abstract that they would want to engage the column there? Yes. Would it -- would the logical unit in my mind be to send a particular police force out in the middle of nowhere, with no connection to anybody else's line, let alone a military force with no connection to anyone's line? I don't believe that that would have been a sound tactical practice under the VRS, that they would have kicked those people out there in isolation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now can we go quickly through something else. We have two more intercepts, and my time is rather limited. And could you please limit your answers to "yes" or "no," if possible at all. Now I would kindly ask you to look at P01148, P01148A and B. The intercept is dated the 13th of July at 1945 and involves unknown persons, X and Y.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already testified about that. In this intercept, the person asking for Ljubisa is not General Krstic, but somebody else who is by General Krstic, at the same place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that person is asking for Ljubisa to report to him personally, to that other person, rather than to General Krstic; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Have Ljubisa call me at General Krstic's." I don't see that as reporting in person, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you obviously don't know who that person is. You don't know who is it who is asking Ljubisa to call him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And besides your indirect conclusion based on the facts that these are the MUP forces, you can't be sure that this is Mr. Borovcanin because the family name Borovcanin is not mentioned at all anywhere?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, you're correct, it's an indirect connection because of the context of MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P00993, the intercept dated 13th July at 2040 hours. And the number, once again, is P00993A and C.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it before you? So let us establish certain things about this document. This intercept allegedly took place an hour after the previous conversation. The previous one took place at 1945, and this one is at 2040; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, if you look at the very beginning of this conversation: "Hello, this Krstic," you will see that Krstic is the one who is calling the other party, who is actually dialing the number, and it is not Borovcanin who is replying, but Krstic is the one who's calling?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that as a fact, because as a matter of their intercept policy, a lot of the switchboard conversation related to who's initiating what call and the route that it's going is not part of the intercepts that they kept because they weren't relevant for the intelligence value. So I don't know that as a fact, who's calling who.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, very well. Furthermore, if you look at the course of the entire conversation, in the body of this text it is not specifically stated that the person is D. Borovcanin from the Special Police. There's no reference to the Borovcanin from the Special. He doesn't introduce himself as, "This is Borovcanin from the Special Police"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you better move to a more substantial --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My next question about this document: Let's for the time being ignore the comment by the person who recorded the intercepted conversation, where it says: "Borovcanin from the Specials," and if we look at the conversation itself, you cannot conclude from the conversation whether this Borovcanin was from the Specials or another Borovcanin, for example, the Borovcanin from the 2nd Romanija Brigade. The body of the conversation, the text, is rather vague. Can you please look at it and see what you think?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to ignore all the other surrounding information that I had, which does in fact put Mr. Borovcanin in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters at this time, I could see in abstract where it could be another Borovcanin. Having said that, I -- I believe this is Ljubomir Borovcanin. I mean, I have to look at it in context of all of the other information that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now just for an assumption's sake, let's assume this is a conversation between General Krstic and Ljubomir Borovcanin. You don't know whether, in the course of the 13th of July, there were maybe some other conversations between these two persons, i.e., Ljubomir Borovcanin and General Krstic; there are no other intercepted conversations that would make you draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, I am not aware of any other intercepts between General Krstic and Mr. Borovcanin or Colonel Borovcanin on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There is no other intercept, either, in which Ljubomir Borovcanin might be involved in any way; isn't that correct? I'm not only referring to the intercepts between himself or a conversation that he might have with General Krstic. I am referring to a conversation between Mr. Borovcanin and anybody else on that day. This is what I'm putting to you, and that's very important.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I agree with you, I don't believe there are any intercepts on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or other intercepts, I should say, than this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just a few more questions and I believe that I will be able to conclude my examination today. In the course of your examination-in-chief, you first said that Mr. Borovcanin, in July 1995, was colonel, and then you corrected yourself and you referred to him as "Mr. Borovcanin." Do you have any reason to correct yourself? Do you have any information about his rank in the police in July 1995, whether there were any ranks in the police at the time? Why did you correct yourself, on what basis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see your point exactly. In -- I think it might have been in either late August or early September of 1995, the MUP established a formal rank system to give it some kind of correspondence with military ranks, and at that point in time Borovcanin was given the rank of -- I believe he was colonel. Now, before that, they did not have a formal rank system and he's always referred to as "Mr." My understanding, of course, in talking to individuals in the post-war environment about this, they always refer to him by the military rank, but of course I'm aware that prior to that August declaration, which established a formalised ranking structure, he didn't hold that as a rank. So I apologise for any confusion that I -- I caused by alternatively referring to him one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's perfectly understandable. I just wanted to clarify this. I have just one more question for you at the end. When you were analysing the documents and as you were preparing your expert reports about the Zepa operation, you did not come by any proof about the participation of any units under the command of Mr. Borovcanin or his participation in the Zepa operation; is that true?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have no information pertaining to Mr. Borovcanin's role in what we would call the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Butler. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I think, Mr. Butler, we'll continue with you on Monday. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are going to decide first the Prosecution confidential urgent motion to add one witness to its 65 ter lists and request for protective -- for a protective order, a motion which was filed on the 22nd of January, 2008, and with which we are seized. We have received oral arguments from the Defence and an oral reply from the Prosecution in the course of today's sitting. The broad test to be applied in these circumstances is whether it would be in the interests of justice to allow the Prosecution to add the witness at this stage of the trial. As we have stated on many occasions, in exercising our discretion, we must balance the Prosecution's duty to present the available evidence to prove its case, with the right of the accused to have adequate time and facilities to prepare a defence and to be tried without undue delay. We are satisfied that the proposed evidence of the witness is prima facie of probative value and relevant to the matters in the indictment. Further, we believe that the Prosecution has diligently pursued the evidence and has disclosed it as soon as practicable. In essence, the application has been brought at this late stage because the Prosecution has only recently located and interviewed the proposed witness. The central issue, therefore, is the possible prejudice to the accused arising from the late stage of the proceedings and the short time they will have available to prepare for cross-examination of the witness. Based on the summary that we have received, we do not agree with the arguments advanced by the Defence, that the proposed evidence changes the nature of the Prosecution case. As to what the indictment does or does not charge, that is a matter for another day. Nevertheless, we are of the opinion that given the short time for the completion of the Prosecution case, there is a real risk that the accused will be prejudiced because of the lack of time to investigate and prepare for the cross-examination of this witness. For this reason, on balance, we feel that it would not be in the interests of justice to grant the Prosecution motion in this respect. However, in the particular circumstances, we believe that this evidence may be ultimately of value to the Trial Chamber. Therefore, following on from the acknowledgment made by one of the Defence counsel earlier on today, the Trial Chamber would give favourable consideration to a Prosecution application to adduce it on rebuttal. To that end, the fact that this evidence was discovered shortly before the close of the Prosecution case will not be considered to the prejudice of the Prosecution if any such application is made in the future. Finally, given the nature of the proposed evidence, we do see validity to the Prosecution's request for a non-disclosure order, provided it is restricted in nature. We therefore order that the contents of and information contained in the interview must not be disclosed in whole or in part to any third party without an application first being made to the Trial Chamber. The third party, however, clearly does not apply to any member of the Defence team, and that includes the investigators of each of the Defence teams who are entitled to receive this information. And that disposes of the said motion. Now, we discussed also earlier on this morning the question of the -- I call them the ICMP or DNA witnesses. We have had discussions. We stand by our previous decision on the Prosecution motion to add two witnesses who have been identified. We're talking of Mr. Parsons and Ms. Tabeau. We have a further decision, however, to communicate to you, and this is as follows: The evidence of these two individuals will be heard in one single day, one single sitting. The Prosecution is to confine itself to the filing or the tendering of the reports or documents of -- or statements of these two witnesses, and we'll have at your disposal a maximum of 30 minutes in the case of each of these two witnesses to put any relevant questions that you may feel necessary. In respect of each of these two witnesses, the Defence will have an hour and a half. That's the -- all of you put together. You're free to decide how you are going to allocate that time amongst yourselves, but you will not have a minute more. We feel that the way this need for these two witnesses originated will also leave unprejudiced any interest that you may have to bring these witnesses as your witnesses later on, as Defence witnesses, if you so wish, but that is our decision. We'll deal with other matters depending on what progress we make in the course of next week. Thank you.
